source.title: cross-site scripting and safe rendering boundaries

mapping.objective: cross-site scripting and safe rendering boundaries
mapping.task_summary: Trace untrusted server/model text to React rendering and verify it is rendered as data rather than executable markup; flag any deliberate HTML escape hatch.

evidence: Learner recognized XSS as a script-injection risk and recalled reflected/stored variants, but initially reversed React's default escaping and dangerouslySetInnerHTML semantics, indicating a material boundary-model gap.

Learner correctly predicted React interpolation renders an HTML-looking payload as inert text, while dangerouslySetInnerHTML creates real DOM markup whose event-handler attribute crosses the data-to-code boundary. A temporary focused React/Vitest check confirmed the DOM distinction; deliberate escape-hatch search found no production dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML/rehypeRaw/javascript: usage in apps/web/src. L4 still requires learner-selected falsifying observation or verification rationale.
